domain: Structural Dynamics of Authority and Agency
topic_summary: Analysis of constraint dynamics in systems with asymmetric power distribution, focusing on how environmental instability, exclusionary coordination mechanisms, and arbitrary enforcement create indexically variant extraction patterns. The formalization demonstrates how identical structural constraints present as different constraint types depending on the observer's power position, exit options, and time horizon.

key_entities: Powerless agents (trapped in immediate time horizon with constrained exit)
Powerful insiders (mobile exit, analytical position, biographical horizon)
Institutional enforcers (negative chi, arbitrage exit, unilateral enforcement capacity)
Moderate identity-locked agents (biographical horizon, normalized extraction)
key_tensions: Indexical variance vs universal classification (same constraint appears as Mountain to some, Rope to others, Snare to others)
Coordination value vs extraction burden (systems providing genuine coordination while extracting asymmetrically)
Enforcer benefit vs subject extraction (institutional positions experience negative chi while subjects experience chi > 1.0)
Immutability perception vs constructed nature (constraints appearing as natural law from trapped indices)
